players.product: Data center leasing to hyperscalers and enterprises (Northern Virginia, Richmond, London, Amsterdam, Mumbai; ~325 MW of leasable capacity energizing over the next 24 months) plus hyperscale and neocloud data center decommissioning

quarterly_data.quarter: Iron Mountain RBC Capital Markets conference 2026 (09-29-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: CEO: beyond the 325 MW of fully permitted, not-yet-leased capacity that gets energized over the next 18-24 months, Iron Mountain has another 300+ MW on additional land that is permitted and committed to be energized by the utilities after that, 200 MW of which is additional capacity coming online in Manassas. The company aims to maintain that 300+ MW of freeboard on an 18- to 24-month rolling basis and continues to build its land bank; CEO: 'If I look forward the next 36-48 months, we feel really good.'
quarterly_data.figure: 325 MW over the next 18-24 months; another 300+ MW after that (200 MW in Manassas)

quarterly_data.quarter: Iron Mountain RBC Capital Markets conference 2026 (09-29-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: CEO: utility power delivery pipelines are 'definitely lengthening' in both North America and Europe, and both have become constrained in capacity (Europe complicated further by balancing renewables); the land Iron Mountain counts as energizing already has committed power, which is why it is acquiring land for the 24 months after that. In India, state governments offer support on power and land to grow data center capacity.

quarterly_data.quarter: Iron Mountain RBC Capital Markets conference 2026 (09-29-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: CEO: Iron Mountain has to date not played in large language model campuses; its capacity is focused on inference, and over 90% of its leasing activity is to the top hyperscalers, typically on 10-15 year leases. CFO: neoclouds and other smaller customers are 5% or so of the portfolio; deals have been written for the last few years at cash-on-cash unlevered returns of about 10%, 11%, 12%; the data center build-out costs somewhere between $9 million-$13 million a megawatt; CFO expects the vast majority of future business to continue with high investment grade cloud hyperscalers.
quarterly_data.figure: over 90% of leasing to top hyperscalers; neoclouds 5% or so; $9 million-$13 million a megawatt

quarterly_data.quarter: Iron Mountain RBC Capital Markets conference 2026 (09-29-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: CEO: Iron Mountain's Middle East data center expansion is through a partnership with Ooredoo, the local telecom operator controlled by the QIA, chosen as an operator that can work with it across the region; the CEO said the partnership 'is working really well'. In India Iron Mountain started with a joint venture, took it to majority by funding the growth and later bought the partner out.

quarterly_data.quarter: Iron Mountain RBC Capital Markets conference 2026 (09-29-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: CFO: Iron Mountain estimates the hyperscale data center decommissioning addressable market at about $3.5 billion based on last year's number and expects it to double to $7 billion in the next four years; cloud hyperscalers refresh gear about every five years, and Iron Mountain wipes and certifies the servers, disassembles them and sells the gear in a revenue share model.
quarterly_data.figure: $3.5 billion TAM, doubling to $7 billion in four years

quarterly_data.quarter: Iron Mountain RBC Capital Markets conference 2026 (09-29-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: CEO: Iron Mountain continues to see 10%+ AFFO per share growth (and has done better so far this year) without using equity; the growth businesses (ALM, data center, digital) are 35% of sales versus 15% when the strategy began, delivering 700 basis points of consolidated growth, heading toward 50%; total TAM for all products and services is $175 billion against sales approaching $8 billion.
quarterly_data.figure: 10%+ AFFO per share growth; growth businesses 35% of sales; $175 billion TAM
